1.title: Limestone: The Core Geology of the Sub-Vosges Hills
1.html: All four limestone Grand Crus sit on the "sub-Vosges hills" (Collines sous-vosgiennes) — the "climatic optimum" zone mentioned in Level 1. The geological base is Muschelkalk (shell limestone) or Dogger (Middle Jurassic) limestone, giving an excellent balance of drainage and water retention.
2.title: The Four Limestone Stars
2.items.0.label: Bruderthal (Molsheim, 18.40 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Upper Muschelkalk plus Lettenkohle limestone / dolomite, uniform marl-limestone soil. Documented as early as 1316 (named by Cistercian monks). Mainly Riesling and Gewurztraminer; Gewurztraminer shows acacia blossom and rose, and Riesling a prominent lasting minerality.
2.items.1.label: Rosacker (Hunawihr, 26.18 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Upper Muschelkalk plus Lettenkohle dolomitic limestone, calcium-magnesium soils. Documented in 1483. Riesling (50%) plus Gewurztraminer (30%). Young Riesling has peppery notes and shows minerality with age; Gewurztraminer has rose and violet aromas.
2.items.2.label: Steinert (Pfaffenheim & Westhalten, 38.90 ha)
2.items.2.desc: Dogger oolitic limestone, dry and extremely permeable, needing rootstocks highly resistant to lime. In 1150 the Benedictines, the Bishop of Basel and the Bishop of Strasbourg all owned vineyards here. Mainly Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Riesling, with aromas especially fully developed with age.
2.items.3.label: Steinklotz (Marlenheim, 40.60 ha)
2.items.3.desc: Meaning "block of stone" — Muschelkalk and dolomitised Keuper "limestone blocks", with topsoil only about 20 cm. In 589 it gave Alsace's earliest written record of wine (Grégoire de Tours)! Pinot Gris, Riesling and Gewurztraminer; noble wines with excellent ageing potential, showing the delicate fruit and spice typical of limestone soils.
3.question: What special place does Steinklotz (Marlenheim) hold in the history of Alsace wine?
3.options.0: It is the only volcanic Grand Cru
3.options.1: A Merovingian-era record of 589, the earliest known written record of wine in Alsace
3.options.2: It is the smallest Grand Cru
3.options.3: It is the only Grand Cru allowed to plant Chardonnay
3.explanation: According to Grégoire de Tours, in 589 the Merovingian king Childebert II owned vineyards at Marlenheim — the earliest known written record of wine in Alsace. Marlenheim is exactly where the limestone Grand Cru Steinklotz lies, giving it a unique pioneering place in Alsace wine history.
4.keyPoints.0: All four limestone sites sit in the sub-Vosges hills, a concrete expression of the "climatic optimum"
4.keyPoints.1: Bruderthal (Molsheim): named by Cistercian monks in 1316, balanced Riesling / Gewurztraminer
4.keyPoints.2: Rosacker (Hunawihr): Riesling (50%) + Gewurztraminer (30%), peppery when young, mineral with age
4.keyPoints.3: Steinert (Pfaffenheim): very dry oolitic limestone needing special lime-resistant rootstocks
4.keyPoints.4: Steinklotz (Marlenheim): site of the earliest known written record of wine in Alsace, in 589
